THE CHECKER'S JOB: verify a finished podcast episode contains its intro/outro bumpers exactly once at expected loudness, via full-lag sample-accurate FFT normalized cross-correlation.

TWO PROVEN DEFECTS, measured on a real episode:
1. MISSED PRESENT BUMPER. Against the real final, the checker reported OUTRO_PRESENCE peak |r|=0.0256 (FAIL). Independent ground truth on the checker's EXACT windows (final tail 38.32s decoded from t=2179.662, mastered outro 33.32s, both mono 8kHz, means subtracted, full-lag FFT cross-correlation, global-energy normalization): r=0.903 at lag +5.042s — the outro audio genuinely starts 5.042s into that window (final t=2184.704, 43ms of AAC priming after the 2184.661 slot). The checker also reported implied_start_s=2184.6606 with a noise-level r, meaning its lag search or its lag->implied-start mapping is wrong: a peak at +5.042s inside the window was invisible to it, while its own self-test passes because every self-test bumper sits at (or a few ms from) the START of its window. Diagnose the actual arithmetic bug — plausible suspects: correlating against only a prefix of the window, wrong sign/branch when splitting the FFT result into positive/negative lags, searching only lags near the expected slot instead of all lags then checking tolerance, or an off-by-window-start in implied_start computation. Fix the real cause; do not band-aid by widening thresholds.
2. EXIT CODE LIES. That run printed OUTRO_PRESENCE FAIL yet the process exited 0. Any FAIL line must produce exit 1 (unusable inputs exit 2). Find why the failure did not propagate and fix it.

REQUIRED SELF-TEST ADDITIONS (--self-test must stay hermetic, ffmpeg lavfi synthesis):
(a) OFFSET-BUMPER CASE shaped like the real defect: build a window where the outro-signature starts ~5s into a segment ~5s longer than the bumper (bumper NOT at window start), AND the assembled final's outro slot computation still expects it there; assert presence PASSes with |r|>=0.9 and the implied start is recovered within 100ms. You MUST first demonstrate red: run the UNFIXED logic path against this case mentally impossible — instead, structure the fix so the new test case provably exercises the changed code path, and print the measured lag it recovers.
(b) EXIT-CODE CASE: invoke the checker's main against the wrong-outro fixture in-process and assert the return/exit code is 1, not just that FAIL text was printed.
Keep every prior self-test case green. Print every case with measured numbers.

Output contract: ./bumper_check.py fixed in place, same CLI as before (--final --intro --outro [--expected-intro-lufs F] [--expected-outro-lufs F] [--lag-tolerance-s] [--min-corr] [--tolerance-lu] [--json] | --self-test). Exit 0 only when everything passes.
